headline: LLMs convert biomedical literature into structured toxicity evidence and knowledge bases
label: Llm Mining Of Toxicology Literature
summary: LLM and RAG pipelines now mine full-text corpora into AOP evidence maps and a 189,212-finding hepatotoxicity knowledge base, alongside integrative graph resources.
synthesis: The dominant thread is LLM-driven extraction of structured toxicological evidence from large literature corpora. AOP-Smart-Finder pairs LLMs with retrieval-augmented generation in a human-AI hybrid framework to map biological events, key event relationships, and AOP evidence. A separate preprint describes an automated, continuous pipeline that mines PubMed/PMC full texts into a hepatotoxicity knowledge base of 189,212 findings across 17,002 chemicals. The shift is toward continuous, corpus-scale curation into queryable structured evidence, with human review retained in the AOP framework. Adjacent items are less directly related: a natural-product atlas built on PPI networks and signed random walks, an infectious-disease knowledge graph in Neo4j, and the KinaseMD 2.0 mutation database. They reflect broader knowledge integration for mechanism and drug response. The summaries do not establish comparative performance across the extraction tools.
